findings.title: All app modules still eagerly imported at module load
findings.body: Each entry is `import("./x")`, which starts loading every app module as soon as the appStore module is evaluated. Nothing is lazy, so startup and bundle cost are not reduced and the PR's goal is not met. The entries should be thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, called on demand by consumers.

findings.title: A failing app import becomes an unhandled rejection at load time
findings.body: The import promises are created eagerly and nothing awaits most of them. If any single app module fails to load (missing env var, syntax error, etc.), its promise rejects with no handler. That produces an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process, even if that app is never used.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in `calendar` field
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async, so `calendar` in each returned item is a Promise rather than a Calendar or null. `getConnectedCalendars` was updated to await it, but other callers of `getCalendarCredentials` that use `item.calendar` directly are not. Those callers will receive a Promise, which is always truthy, so null checks pass and method calls on it fail.

findings.title: forEach(async) pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
findings.body: The async forEach callback now awaits `getCalendar` before reaching `apiDeletes.push`. By the time it pushes, `Promise.all(apiDeletes)` has already run, so these deletions for recurring bookings are never awaited. Any errors from them become unhandled rejections.

findings.title: forEach(async) makes calendar deletions fire-and-forget
findings.body: Calendar and video deletions now run inside an async forEach callback whose promise is ignored. Failures surface as unhandled rejections rather than being reported to the caller. The same pattern in vital and wipemycalother reschedule.ts also makes their surrounding try/catch ineffective. Use `await Promise.all(map(...))` instead.
